STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple on a white plate, photographed from directly above (top-down).

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish side/dinner plate about 24 cm across, so its area is roughly 480 cm² (corners are rounded and the sides curve in, so call it about 450 cm²). The apple is about 130 px wide against a plate about 360 px wide, which gives roughly 8.5 cm.

STEP 3 - Items: One red-yellow apple.

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's footprint is π × 4.25² ≈ 57 cm², about 12% of the plate. The food covers about 12% of the vessel in total.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple of 8.5 cm diameter is a sphere of about 4/3 × π × 4.25³ ≈ 320 ml. Apples are slightly flattened, so I use about 300 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole apple density is about 0.8 g/ml, which gives about 240 g. With the core included, a typical apple of this size weighs 200–230 g, so I use about 215 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple is about 52 kcal/100 g, so 215 g gives about 112 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A medium-large apple of about 215 g and about 110 kcal is plausible, and nothing else is on the plate.
